newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, South Africa aim to complete talks in 1998.
newsitem.headline: EU, South Africa aim to complete talks in 1998.

text.p: The European Union and South Africa said on Friday they aimed to complete their protracted technical discussions on a bilateral trade and development pact sometime in 1998.
South Africa said in June it hoped to complete the talks by the end of 1997, but the announcement suggests that was seen as unrealistic.

EU Development Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro and South African Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin told reporters they had agreed a framework for resolving stumbling blocks that have held up progress.
"We have been able to identify processes and mechanisms that take us forward more rapidly," Erwin said.

The often heated EU-South African talks, which began in 1994, have faltered on several issues, notably Europe's desire to exclude about 40 percent of South Africa's agricultural products from the deal and the effects of a free trade area on South Africa's neighbours.

Deus Pinheiro and Erwin gave few details about how they would move the talks forward, but issued a joint statement reaffirming their intent to set up a free trade area in all sectors with a transition period of 12 years.
They said they would also agree cooperation in areas including political dialogue, industry, development, science and technology.

They acknowledged that certain sensitive sectors and products -- including textiles, according to Erwin -- would require special treatment and agreed to negotiate separate accords on wine and spirits and on fisheries.

They also agreed that the EU would eliminate its bilateral tariffs faster than South Africa and that the 12 members of the Southern African Development Community would have equal or better access to the South African market than the EU.
